thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Cuts Losses as Tech Storms Back

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Intraday Update: Dow Cuts Losses as Tech Storms Back
text:
By Ben Levisohn Updated Aug. 2, 2018 12:58 p.m. ET No Worries. Yes, tariffs are back in the headlines , but the Dow Jones Industrial Average was off its worst levels while the S&P 500 was actually trading higher. Apple (AAPL) became the first U.S. company to reach a $1 trillion market value , only to slip back immediately. In today's Intraday Update , we...
Illustration: Getty Images •...wonder whether the value resurgence is over already;
•...review U.S. Steel's (X) earnings;
•...explain why T-Mobile US (TMUS) is up nearly 4%.
Tariffs Are No Value So much for the value resurgence .
With trade wars making headlines again, the S&P 500 is little changed at 2814.29 at 11:58 a.m. today, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has dropped 109.28 points, or 0.4%, to 25,224.54. The Nasdaq Composite has gained 0.5% to 7,748.31.
Tech stocks, which had been getting hit following Facebook's (FB) earnings disappointment , are higher today, with the S&P 500 Information Technology Index up 1.1%.Value stocks, however, are underperforming the market, as materials, energy, financials, and industrials are all falling today. The iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF (IWD) had gained 0.2% to $124.49. The Value ETF had gained 0.2% from July 25 through Aug. 1, 1.3 percentage points better than the SPDR S&P 500 ETF's (SPY) 1.1% decline, prompting some observers to call a turn in favor of value . It may still happen, but value is still in a downtrend relative to the overall market.
What might give value a boost? The strategists at Pavilion Global Markets point to the shift from away from monetary stimulus toward fiscal stimulus. They note that as central banks wind down their easy-monetary policy, governments are spending more, with the U.S. tax cuts just the most obvious example. China, for instance, is taking steps to ensure its economy remains strong .
"The removal of monetary accommodation suggests that the outperformance of long-duration assets (i.e. long bonds vs. commodities and Growth vs. Value stocks) will revert to more normal levels," they write.
Maybe that's the case, but we'd still like to see that downtrend break first.
Midday Movers Apple (AAPL) is up 2.4% to $206.29, as its market capitalization passed the $1 trillion mark for the first time earlier today.
McDonald's (MCD) is down 2.1% to $153.71 after reports from Business Insider about listeria at some of its restaurants .
T-Mobile US (TMUS) is up 3.9% to $61.67 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The wireless carrier earned 92 cents a share on revenue of $10.57 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of 86 cents a share on revenue of $10.65 billion.
Red Robin Gourmet Burgers (RRGB) is down 19.7% to $36.83 after it provided disappointing preliminary second-quarter results and was downgraded to Market Perform by Raymond James.
U.S. Steel (X) is down 9.8% to $32.31 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The steelmaker earned $1.46 a share on revenue of $3.61 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.12 on revenue of $3.47 billion. — Teresa Rivas
